description: Game engine for Santase (known as 66, Сантасе, Sixty-six, Sechsundsechzig or Schnapsen), the fast two-player trick-taking card game played with 24 cards: the Ace, Ten, King, Queen, Jack and Nine of each suit. Plays whole matches between bots, or one move at a time with per-seat views and replayable match records for user interfaces and game servers.
releaseNotes:
3.0.0 (the first release since 2.0.0 in 2018)

New
- SantaseMatch: a match driven one action at a time that never waits for a player (Start, ToMove, Act, Validate, Stop), for user interfaces and game servers. SantaseGame, which plays a whole match between two IPlayers, now runs on it.
- Per-seat views (SantaseSeatView) and match records (SantaseMatchRecord) as plain models. A view never shows the opponent's hand and rebuilds the exact PlayerTurnContext; a record replays the match exactly.
- IRestorablePlayer: a bot rebuilds its memory from a view, so no bot object has to live between moves.
- An injectable random source for every deal (SantaseMatchOptions.Shuffle, SantaseGame, Deck) with a documented deal order.
- CardCode: cards as short text codes (9C, 10D, JH, QS, KC, AH).
- CardWinnerLogic.GetWinner: the trick-winner rule as a static method.

Rules and fixes
- The +10 for the last trick is awarded only when all 24 cards are played and nobody closed.
- The round phases follow the talon, so rule variants with other deal sizes play correctly; SantaseMatch refuses rules no match can play.
- A move with no action or no card is rejected as invalid instead of crashing, and the engine always computes a move's announce itself.
- Card.GetCard and Card.FromHashCode throw for anything that is not a Santase card; CardCollection rejects null.

Performance
- About 2x the engine throughput of 2.0.0 and far fewer allocations: allocation-free CardCollection enumeration, incremental round points, an in-place shuffle.

Breaking changes
- Targets .NET 10 (was .NET Standard 2.0).
- Removed RandomProvider and EnumerableExtensions.Shuffle (pass a random source instead). Card is sealed. IRoundWinnerPointsLogic.GetWinnerPoints takes the last trick's winner.
- PlayerActionValidator.GetPossibleCardsToPlay returns a CardCollection for a CardCollection hand; it is still typed ICollection<Card>, so do not cast it to List<Card>.
